questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic level, distance from home country, familiarity in culture, city with many opportunities

questions.answer: Difficult, Join a housing site and don't be picky, watch out for scammers

questions.answer: It's expensive if you want to live in the city

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: there were multiple rounds of registration and application for courses, the info was very limited

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I e-mailed them multiple times for answers about the process

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful, I got what I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe speak with others who are also going there to make sure you didn't miss anything

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My course were not difficult but the workload was more than I'm used to. Some of my courses were completely open to everyone and therefore very basic. A lot of repetition from my previous studies

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Differs, but generally more of a high school kind of teaching, some will even point you out to say something even though you didn't put your hand up

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: urban studies, development and globalisation, global political economy, environment and development, identity, diversity and inclusion

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: development and globalisation will give you a whole new perspective on the world

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: pretty easy, there are a lot of migrants and expats so its very multicultural

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the dutch are a bit closed off

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: that it's multicultural

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. don't worry about grades, people don't do that as much as they do at KU (in my experience)
2. it's an amazing city with so many opportunities, explore as much as you can
3. for a good social experience: be spontaneous, take initiative and let your fear of rejection stay at home

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: don't stress, it'll all work out :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Friendships and experiences

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning it was a bit hard not having that "safety-person" around that you know you can always come to. But remember that everyone is in the same boat, don't be scared to reach out.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
